s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital and facial syndrome with mass effect
key_facts: History of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
Treated with 4 cycles of ABVC followed by 3060 cGY at the neck and mediastinum
Left upper eyelid mass excised on 3 separate occasions
Painless proptosis developed four months later
Left-sided facial numbness developed seventeen months later
Histopathology showed multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
MRI showed lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Genetic testing demonstrated a splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the PALB2 gene

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital and facial syndrome with mass effect
key_facts: History of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
Treated with 4 cycles of ABVC followed by 3060 cGY at the neck and mediastinum
Left upper eyelid mass excised on 3 separate occasions

Left-sided facial numbness developed seventeen months later
Histopathology showed multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells

MRI showed lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Genetic testing demonstrated a splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the PALB2 gene

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, positive for CD68

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology and imaging findings consistent with this rare histiocytic disorder

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, although immunohistochemistry negative for CD45 and S100

shortlist.label: Histiocytic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive clinical course and histopathology findings, including increased mitotic activity

shortlist.label: Tenosynovial giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Giant cell rich tumor with potential for local aggression and recurrence

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a painless, left upper eyelid mass, proptosis, and subsequent left-sided facial numbness, along with histopathology showing a multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, and immunohistochemistry positive for CD68, is consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease. The involvement of the orbit and extension into the intracranial compartment also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with lymphadenopathy and does not usually involve the orbit

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with lytic bone lesions and does not usually have the characteristic multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like giant cells

rejected.label: Histiocytic sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms and does not usually have the characteristic orbital involvement

rejected.label: Tenosynovial giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Typically presents with a localized tumor in the joints or tendons and does not usually involve the orbit
